I’m going to say what too many politicians won’t: What’s happening in Washington isn’t normal — and it’s hurting families here at home.
While Coloradans are worrying about grocery bills, healthcare costs, and whether they’ll ever be able to retire with dignity, our representative is busy chasing outrage, breaking rules, and embarrassing this district on a national stage.
Lauren Boebert calls it “fighting.” I call it failing — failing to show up for rural communities, to deliver for small businesses, and to understand how hard life has gotten for working families.
It’s time for a change. That’s why I’m running to defeat Lauren Boebert.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trisha-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trisha-dsg-email?]
I’m Trisha Calvarese. I grew up here, I went to public schools here, and when my parents were both battling cancer at the same time, I came home to take care of them.
I’ve spent my career fighting for working people — from representing 12.5 million union members to helping secure historic investments in American manufacturing, clean energy, and innovation that are creating good-paying jobs right here in Colorado.
I know what serious leadership looks like. And every day, Lauren Boebert chooses headlines over hard work and stunts over solutions.
Washington insiders are betting she can keep getting away with it. But they’re wrong. This race is winnable. It can flip the House and send a message that Colorado won’t tolerate another term of chaos, cruelty, and incompetence.
But only if we fight back — together. So if you’re ready for a hometown candidate who shows up, tells the truth, and puts working families first, I’m asking you to chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can right now. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trisha-dsg-email?]

I grew up here, I went to public schools here, and when my parents were both battling cancer at the same time, I came home to take care of them. I’ve spent my career fighting for working people — from representing 12.5 million union members to helping secure historic investments in American manufacturing, clean energy, and innovation that are creating good-paying jobs right here in Colorado. I know what serious leadership looks like. And every day, Lauren Boebert chooses headlines over hard work and stunts over solutions. Washington insiders are betting she can keep getting away with it. But they’re wrong. This race is winnable. It can flip the House and send a message that Colorado won’t tolerate another term of chaos, cruelty, and incompetence. But only if we fight back — together. So if you’re ready for a hometown candidate who shows up, tells the truth, and puts working families first, I’m asking you to chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can right now. Yes, the amount we’re able to fundraise over these next few days is extremely important for a campaign as competitive as ours. But I’m not sending this note just to ask for your donation. I also want to take a moment to be real with you about what’s at stake — and to thank you for everything you’ve done to get us here.
My path to Congress wasn’t exactly conventional. I was raised by a single mom and was the first in my family to attend college. I worked multiple jobs to pay my way through school. And I started my career working in economic and community development on Native American reservations —and yes, I even had a brief stint as a professional MMA fighter somewhere in between!
When I decided to run for Kansas’ 3rd in 2018, a lot of pundits thought our campaign wouldn’t even get off the ground.
Slowly but surely, we gained support though. We took that campaign to every corner of the district — speaking with thousands of Kansans about the issues that matter. Folks told their neighbors about our campaign — and those neighbors told their loved ones. All of a sudden, we had the momentum. We had the grassroots power to flip an entrenched Republican district on Election Day.
**That didn’t happen because of big donors.** It happened because people like you chipped in five, ten, twenty dollars and believed it could make a difference, and it did.
Those contributions helped bring tens of thousands of good jobs to Kansas’ 3rd. They helped pass the most significant gun safety law in a generation. They brought in millions of dollars for local infrastructure projects, flood resilience, health care access, and so much more.

clean_body: = Hey, it’s Sharice. I’ll keep this simple: We need to hit our $15,000 fundraising goal before our Sunday night deadline, and I’m writing to ask for your help. = | | = Yes, the amount we’re able to fundraise over these next few days is extremely important for a campaign as competitive as ours. But I’m not sending this note just to ask for your donation. I also want to take a moment to be real with you about what’s at stake — and to thank you for everything you’ve done to get us here. My path to Congress wasn’t exactly conventional. I was raised by a single mom and was the first in my family to attend college. I worked multiple jobs to pay my way through school. And I started my career working in economic and community development on Native American reservations —and yes, I even had a brief stint as a professional MMA fighter somewhere in between! When I decided to run for Kansas’ 3rd in 2018, a lot of pundits thought our campaign wouldn’t even get off the ground. Slowly but surely, we gained support though. We took that campaign to every corner of the district — speaking with thousands of Kansans about the issues that matter. Folks told their neighbors about our campaign — and those neighbors told their loved ones. All of a sudden, we had the momentum. We had the grassroots power to flip an entrenched Republican district on Election Day. That didn’t happen because of big donors. It happened because people like you chipped in five, ten, twenty dollars and believed it could make a difference, and it did. Those contributions helped bring tens of thousands of good jobs to Kansas’ 3rd. They helped pass the most significant gun safety law in a generation. They brought in millions of dollars for local infrastructure projects, flood resilience, health care access, and so much more. But there’s still so much left to do. Families and farmers need real support, costs are too high, and we need an economy that’s built from the ground up — not handed down from the top. And the only way we can do it? body:
Texans are tired of working more and getting less
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
**We’re about to flip a deep red district, Peter.**
A new poll just showed that we’re tied with Greg Abbott in TX-23 — a district he won by 10 points in 2022 and Trump won by 15 points in 2024.
This is huge, Peter. Not only did Democrats outvote Republicans in a midterm primary for the first time in 24 years, but Abbott’s support is plummeting.
I’ve been traveling across the state, meeting voters where they are, and everywhere I go, I hear the same thing:**Texans are tired of working more and getting less because they’re paying the Greg Abbott Corruption Tax.**
Voters in districts like this are telling us they’re ready for change — they’re rejecting the corruption that has made Greg Abbott and a few of his billionaire buddies rich while the rest of us pay the price.
This campaign isn’t about left vs. right, it’s about electing a governor that will put working families first by fighting for strong schools, lower costs, and a Texas that actually works for Texans.
We’re still in a statistical tie with Greg Abbott statewide, and with momentum like this, I know we can win in November.

Hi there, it’s Adam Schiff.
There is still a lot we don’t know about the remaining Epstein Files, but there’s something we know for sure: **this administration can’t stop lying**.
From Donald Trump to Pam Bondi to Kash Patel and Howard Lutnick, and countless others — they're all a pack of liars.
Despite their boasting and claims that they were more than prepared to release the files, they have continued to conceal damning information about influential people who victimized young girls.
They also lied about the scope of the files left unreleased — claiming that it was because they wanted to protect the victims. And yet, the files were released without even redacting all their information — _including names and nude photographs_ — which only further victimized them.
We have to stand up to this abuse of power, to defend our country and its people. To demand justice and accountability. To fight back. I have and I always will. Because this fight isn’t over. It’s just beginning, and I won’t back down.

subject: What does healthcare mean to YOU? Take TOP’s survey! / ¿Qué significa la atención médica para ti? ¡Participa en la encuesta de TOP! 📋 📝
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/PNG%202023%20TOP%20Newsletter%20Header.png]
Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
SHARE YOUR THOUGHTS:
Tell us what you'd like to change about our healthcare system
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Make%20your%20voice%20heard.png]
This is YOUR chance to weigh in!
Trump’s second term has been a complete mess for healthcare access and affordability. From higher health insurance premium costs, to massive cuts to Medicaid, Texans of all walks of life are feeling the negative impacts.
At TOP, we view healthcare as a human right , and with our healthcare system in the abysmal shape it is, we want to hear from YOU – members, supporters, and community allies.
Tell us what REAL healthcare looks like to you, and share your personal story.
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfoc1OUiuz2TfuWAMFfFO2p2m3ti1xB9QGZzEjIya3BgLA9EA/viewform [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfoc1OUiuz2TfuWAMFfFO2p2m3ti1xB9QGZzEjIya3BgLA9EA/viewform]
ROOTED IN POWER:
TOP joins national allies in honoring Bloody Sunday at annual Selma Bridge Crossing Jubilee
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Selma%20weekend%202026.jpg]
An unforgettable weekend: TOP Executive Director Brianna Brown along with members Josie Smith and John Valdez joined our national affiliate Popular Democracy in Selma, Alabama, for this year’s inspiring Selma Jubilee [https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/picture-gallery/news/2026/03/08/selma-bridge-crossing-jubilee-honors-61st-anniversary-of-bloody-sunday/89056067007/] honoring the 61st anniversary of the crossing of the Edmund Pettus Bridge on Bloody Sunday.
Tens of thousands of people from across the country and world gathered in Selma to commemorate the courageous lengths that civil rights leaders and freedom fighters went through to secure and win the Voting Rights Act of 1965 . This was also the first Jubilee without civil rights giant Rev. Jesse Jackson (Rest in power).
TOP's collective message with Popular Democracy at this transformational event focused on our need to defend the 14th Amendment from insidious right-wing attacks. This amendment is being targeted by the likes of MAGA-aligned think tanks and the White House because it guarantees that everyone born or naturalized in our country is a citizen, entitled to equal protection under the law. The promise in this amendment has shaped every major civil rights victory in our nation.
Read up on how the 14th Amendment impacts everyday life for MILLIONS here in the U.S. [https://nonprofitquarterly.org/why-we-must-defend-the-fourteenth-amendment/]
LAST CALL:
Vote for TOP to host a panel at Netroots Nation 2026
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Netroots%20Nation%202026%20Philly.png]
VOTE BY FRIDAY! - TOP applied to host a panel at Netroots Nation this year, and we'd appreciate your VOTE to make this panel a reality. The deadline to vote is Friday, March 13.
It'll take you less than a minute to show your support, and it'll get us closer to sharing TOP's theory of change on the national stage with hundreds of progressive activists and organizers from across the country.
Just follow these quick steps:
1. Check out our panel topic, "Texas: MAGA before MAGA and how we can still win!" [https://netrootsnation.secure-platform.com/nn26/gallery/rounds/82014/details/12779]
2. Click on the blue "Vote for this submission" button.
3. Create a new account if you need to, or log in to your existing Netroots account.
4. Select our panel and vote!
Feel free to share the panel link on your social media, and use the hashtag #NN26.
Shouting-out a TOP board president turned staff member, and a longtime San Antonio change-maker
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Dr.%20Doshie%20Piper%20-%20SA%20Mag.jpg]
Dr. Doshie Piper's contributions to the people of San Antonio and our movement have been abundant — from her vast knowledge of issues impacting our communities, to the deep commitment she has to our collective liberation.
A criminal justice professor at the University of the Incarnate Word, Dr. Piper served as TOP's board president and co-president for six years, helping oversee and grow our organization from 2019 to 2025. We are now ecstatic to have her serving on staff with us as TOP Restorative Justice Coordinator.
READ her feature in San Antonio Magazine, as she was included in its Women Shaping San Antonio edition. [https://www.sanantoniomag.com/dream-big-doshie-piper-criminal-justice-restorative-justice-mlk/]
TRUMP TRACKER:
His MAGA propaganda machine is gaining power and threatening our future
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Disinformation.jpg]
Disinformation was a centerpiece of Trump 1.0. The man proved to the entire world what millions of us already knew: that he’s a racist egotistical liar unfit to hold office.
It was disinformation that contributed to his return to power, and fast-forward to now, Trump 2.0 has shown us all in real time what disinformation ON STEROIDS looks like, with AI and media-owning oligarchs playing a big role in amplifying and normalizing his authoritarian message.
What’s even more alarming now is that Trump and his regime have attempted to go after people simply for calling out his rampant disinformation! [https://www.techpolicy.press/fantasy-becomes-reality-as-trump-takes-revenge-on-disinformation-researchers/]
So what’s the difference in how Trump is weaponizing disinformation now than before? It’s the massive communication apparatus that’s now in place to support him. [https://btlonline.org/trump-aligned-oligarchs-media-mergers-transforming-outlets-into-maga-propaganda-platforms-2/]
Huge media deals have been made in the last few weeks by some of the wealthiest men in the world, and it’s not by accident.
Trump 2.0 paved the way for this, and it’s already having consequences, as faith in journalism is plummeting and newsrooms at historically reputable publications are cutting reporters and shedding fact-checkers. [https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/02/11/majority-of-americans-express-low-confidence-in-journalists-to-act-in-publics-best-interests/]
Español
COMPARTE TUS OPINIONES:
Cuéntanos qué te gustaría cambiar de nuestro sistema de salud
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Levanta%20Tu%20Voz.png]
¡Esta es TU oportunidad de opinar!
El segundo mandato de Trump ha sido un completo desastre para el acceso y la asequibilidad de la atención médica. Desde el aumento de las primas del seguro médico hasta los recortes masivos a Medicaid, los tejanos de todos los ámbitos están sintiendo las consecuencias negativas.
En TOP, consideramos la atención médica como un derecho humano , y con nuestro sistema de salud en tan mal estado, queremos saber de USTEDES: miembros, simpatizantes y aliados de la comunidad.
Cuéntanos cómo sería para ti una atención médica de verdad y comparte tu historia personal.
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf1bY_DlK7WwjhHEWsdJhb8yQSqAUdL3z_EEH_QepPF2HeAEw/viewform [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf1bY_DlK7WwjhHEWsdJhb8yQSqAUdL3z_EEH_QepPF2HeAEw/viewform]
ARRAIGADO EN EL PODER: TOP se une a aliados nacionales para honrar el Domingo Sangriento en el Jubileo anual del Cruce del Puente de Selma
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Selma%20weekend%202026.jpg]
Un fin de semana inolvidable: La directora ejecutiva de TOP, Brianna Brown, junto con los miembros Josie Smith y John Valdez, se unieron a nuestra filial nacional, Popular Democracy, en Selma, Alabama, para el inspirador Jubileo de Selma [https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/picture-gallery/news/2026/03/08/selma-bridge-crossing-jubilee-honors-61st-anniversary-of-bloody-sunday/89056067007/] de este año, en honor al 61.o aniversario del cruce del Puente Edmund Pettus el Domingo Sangriento.
Decenas de miles de personas de todo el país y del mundo se reunieron en Selma para conmemorar la valentía de los líderes de los derechos civiles y los luchadores por la libertad para conseguir y obtener la Ley de Derecho al Voto de 1965 . Este también fue el primer Jubileo sin el gigante de los derechos civiles, el reverendo Jesse Jackson (que descanse en paz).
El mensaje colectivo de TOP con Popular Democracy en este evento transformador se centró en nuestra necesidad de defender la 14.a Enmienda de los insidiosos ataques de la derecha. Esta enmienda está siendo criticada por grupos de expertos alineados con MAGA y la Casa Blanca, porque garantiza que toda persona nacida o naturalizada en nuestro país sea ciudadana, con derecho a la misma protección ante la ley. La promesa de esta enmienda ha dado forma a cada victoria importante en materia de derechos civiles en nuestra nación.
Infórmese sobre cómo la 14.a Enmienda impacta la vida cotidiana de MILLONES de personas aquí en EE. UU. [https://nonprofitquarterly.org/why-we-must-defend-the-fourteenth-amendment/]
ÚLTIMA OPORTUNIDAD:
Vota por TOP para organizar un panel en Netroots Nation 2026
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Netroots%20Nation%202026%20Philly.png]
¡VOTA ANTES DEL VIERNES! TOP solicitó ser anfitrión de un panel en Netroots Nation este año, y agradeceríamos tu VOTO para que este panel se haga realidad. La fecha límite para votar es el viernes 13 de marzo.
Te tomará menos de un minuto mostrar tu apoyo y nos acercará a compartir la teoría del cambio de TOP a nivel nacional con cientos de activistas y organizadores progresistas de todo el país.
Solo sigue estos pasos:
1. Consulta el tema de nuestro panel: "Texas: ¡MAGA antes de MAGA y cómo aún podemos ganar!" [https://netrootsnation.secure-platform.com/nn26/gallery/rounds/82014/details/12779]
2. Haz clic en el botón azul "Vota por esta propuesta."
3. Crea una nueva cuenta si lo necesitas o inicia sesión en tu cuenta de Netroots.
4. ¡Selecciona nuestro panel y vota!
Comparte el enlace del panel en tus redes sociales y usa la etiqueta #NN26.
Felicitando a una presidente de la junta directiva de TOP que se convirtió en miembro del personal y una campeóna de San Antonio desde hace mucho tiempo
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Dr.%20Doshie%20Piper%20-%20SA%20Mag.jpg]
Las contribuciones de la Dra. Doshie Piper a la gente de San Antonio y a nuestro movimiento han sido abundantes , desde su vasto conocimiento de los problemas que afectan a nuestras comunidades hasta su profundo compromiso con nuestra liberación colectiva.
Profesora de justicia penal en la Universidad del Verbo Encarnado, la Dra. Piper fue presidenta y copresidenta de la junta directiva de TOP durante seis años, contribuyendo a la supervisión y el crecimiento de nuestra organización de 2019 a 2025. Nos complace enormemente contar con ella como Coordinadora de Justicia Restaurativa de TOP.
LEA su artículo en la revista San Antonio Magazine, ya que fue incluida en su edición "Mujeres que Forjan San Antonio." [https://www.sanantoniomag.com/dream-big-doshie-piper-criminal-justice-restorative-justice-mlk/]
RASTREADOR DE TRUMP:
Su maquinaria de propaganda MAGA está ganando poder y amenaza nuestro futuro
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Disinformation.jpg]
La desinformación fue un elemento central del Trump 1.0. Este hombre demostró al mundo entero lo que millones de nosotros ya sabíamos: que es un mentiroso racista y egoísta, incapaz de ejercer un cargo.
Fue la desinformación lo que contribuyó a su regreso al poder , y ahora, Trump 2.0 nos está mostrando en tiempo real cómo se ve la desinformación al extremo, con la IA y los oligarcas dueños de medios desempeñando un papel clave al amplificar y normalizar su mensaje autoritario.
Lo que es aún más alarmante ahora es que Trump y su régimen han intentado perseguir a la gente simplemente por denunciar su desinformación desenfrenada. [https://www.techpolicy.press/fantasy-becomes-reality-as-trump-takes-revenge-on-disinformation-researchers/]
Entonces, ¿cuál es la diferencia en cómo Trump está utilizando la desinformación ahora en comparación con antes? No injuries were reported at either location, but the attacks follow Iranian drone strikes on U.S. facilities in Riyadh and Dubai, underscoring the growing danger facing American outposts worldwide. ★★★
BREAKING: Terror Strikes Twice on American Soil

A convicted ISIS supporter opened fire Thursday morning inside an ROTC classroom at [Old Dominion University](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2O4yAUhZ8Gd7bwxYG4oNiGLttuaWEg9tXCxTLEaN5-lEjzAtOd5vx8599jeViMSNtfm4J2Fy4--6W8yhFcRcrR-5yQMNOL8AoLcJA9F_0IC8Vl7Lx2Xgrogh6VEuI2ca66XXs_ruC4sk7dZzc79Zylsl5aeN7sJFSH-p3ExQgAwPk0uPsMclrBzStwLlc28dfhbQ1lcJlKOC9b8QpIlN8q0-By6qLeaz0KE38YGAamtTY0W3akrWaqmD72xMBQaIWBebcyMMmeDMwIDEzZc65IW5-j739g-w_tWbB-9f8pNwamO7U_GsaIRSo28S1ZjJ8R9Re_XRq-AwAA__8YBX4W) in Norfolk, Virginia, killing a retired Army officer and wounding two other military-affiliated victims before being stabbed to death by an ROTC cadet. The FBI identified the gunman as [Mohamed Bailor Jalloh](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE8DnVfwwHi3oEhDt2lTWvyun4TBMtir3D5ypFwg3YxGmk8zX8_5aTFjeX3aNWp_4hxqmNvRtug7lppDqCsWrOUoeMYZGKiBiYHDXPLMadA-KAE0aj5NQoySsYkuWvgEd86dEylZ5QWPScloU_JcOgWOor6amOAAAIzJm78_QEkH_uGAMeWIZMcWbI_t5mtpcT9txzNiKfVStdx8XWnWS-9bI-KDgCFgen2XxeZ8hZfFrS0xdgLGrt-DP_aOjYC52AQMEwQMBwKm5jD8DR3aUmuP-1BATTCNI9112N6YMzY1Ecleq8VfAu3_eOzU8BMAAP__pQN6BA), 36, a former Virginia National Guardsman who pled guilty in 2016 to providing material support to ISIS and was released from federal prison in December 2024. The FBI is investigating the attack as [an act of terrorism](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLFuwyAURb8Gb1j44UAyMHTxlq4dLczD8aswzwrEbv--StT-QLcrXelenfNxHa-eEuXbu1-jCzuNyDiWR9liqJQ5IfJKmTg_Mu1xBAVGKi07GHMauwZdQKOhia6zVutTr5RtFjfhPEXUppttr6w6n4L1Js7hHM2krcGG3HNJ6Q4AQKm-DecLmH6CcJlAKTOJXj029DWWNnAu8b77SnuknPmZOLeB1ya5pdatCP0mYBAwHMfRzvx1wvCsBQw5HkXAsPLi14jy06fEi-SE8o9LvsDuheq3LAtzpXyTvwIkFSrN3eF2UEpUjBW9uq2e0uu9_kPY7uAnAAD__9jtfic). Hours later, a suspect rammed an explosives-laden truck into [Temple Israel](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOszAQhJ8GOqNlTYAULv4mXf72SmS8S7KS8SLswD3-iXuE60aa0czo-3pOTy9R0uu_X9mFQyZSmvInbxyKJI1EukoSTZ8kB08I2BuwpsUpxamtyQXqLdbs2mGw9tYBDPXb2QVGOy5IALdxoT4QwDx6Ggem-22xtbirCWyLiAjQNWG8Y9_NGO4zAvRz1cFnI184N0FT5v3wRQ6WlPRSmpqgax3du5QtV_ZfhY8KH-d5Not-I3HZVcqVqfCR-MyXybmYOaqui3Aks2mUwGbnvGkiSS_jw7VhcuDEpvC6RTaSd8-x3h1tp8QouR-qDl6rl_h7ofyB2uHwJwAA__8A73-d) in West Bloomfield, Michigan -- the nation's largest Reform synagogue -- before opening fire with a rifle. Synagogue security shot and killed the attacker; all 140 preschool students and staff escaped unharmed. Law enforcement [found mortar-type](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0D2uqzAQBeDVmM5oGBycFC5eQ5fX3hL5Z5KMZGwLG9j-FVnC7UYjnU9H5-e5PC1HTu__diXjD15CDkvdayHfOOUYQl45cU574oMWBJwkjHLAJcVl6ILxYRqxIzNoPY43BaC7j3GIergB3Ohl4Q7eDSGQcgpeD6f0XXdsLgnGARERQPX-_sBJOfQPhwCTEwr2Emyj2vucKm2HbXwQp5SvK6fe57WL5tNaqWL8J3AWOJ_n2XtXE51XbBU4B2pb5iZwvp4C55Ije5Ib1ZJTkNZfrKyfnBttsnLbv7y0TTZaSyTJdbMUBc7dZkI5OUaukxYK3qvl-O3R_jDdYfA3AAD__wD9gJQ) explosives inside the suspect's vehicle, and the body was badly burned. FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed agents are on scene at both locations. clean_body: | Hi friends, The right to vote is a key part of the foundation of our democracy, but it only works if we protect it. Right now, Trump and his MAGA cronies are pushing the SAVE Act, which would create new barriers to voter registration by requiring additional proof of citizenship and making it harder for millions of eligible Americans to register or update their information. While they pretend this is a reasonable step to prevent voter fraud, we know the truth. Whenever new voting restrictions are imposed, fewer people vote, regardless of the fact that they’re perfectly eligible to do so. This attack isn’t Trump’s first attempt to undermine democracy, and it won’t be the last. While we continue the fight to elect leaders who will fight back against this administration, there is one important step you can take right now. Take a minute to check your voter registration. It only takes a minute, but it ensures that when the time comes to vote, you won’t be turned away because your registration has suddenly been purged. Please take a moment to check your registration today and consider sharing the link with friends and family so they can do the same. Our democracy works best when everyone can participate. # Active shooter with bomb laden truck hits Michigan synagogue
A gunman rammed an explosive-laden truck[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ea96f214-8aa0-45f8-9f46-806a3f034206?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[into Temple Israel synagogue](https://substack.com/redirect/ea96f214-8aa0-45f8-9f46-806a3f034206?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in West Bloomfield, Michigan, on Thursday, then opened fire before being killed in a shootout with security. Students and staff were reportedly unharmed in the attack.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ea96f214-8aa0-45f8-9f46-806a3f034206?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Security 's Swift Response**: Synagogue armed guards immediately engaged the intruder in gunfire after he crashed through the building and began shooting, neutralizing the threat and preventing further casualties beyond minor injury to one guard struck by the vehicle.
* **Explosives Discovery** : Authorities recovered a large quantity of explosives from the suspect's truck, which caught fire post-crash, prompting bomb technicians and extensive sweeps to clear the scene and ensure no additional devices remained.
* **Community-Wide Precautions** : Michigan State Police boosted patrols at other houses of worship while the Jewish Federation of Detroit placed affiliated agencies on precautionary lockdown to safeguard members during the unfolding investigation.
* **Official Reactions** : Governor Gretchen Whitmer condemned the attack as heartbreaking, emphasizing peaceful practice of faith, while FBI personnel joined local forces on scene to probe the motive and potential accomplices in early stages.

# **Heroic ROTC student fatally stabs ISIS-linked gunman who opened fire at Old Dominion University, saving lives**
A heroic ROTC student **[fatally stabbed ISIS-linked gunman](https://substack.com/redirect/e102172f-8135-421a-a203-53046233e630?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Mohamed Bailor Jalloh, 36, after he walked into an Old Dominion University classroom Thursday, asked if it was an ROTC class, and opened fire, killing a retired military instructor and wounding two other Army ROTC members. FBI Director Kash Patel said "the shooter is now deceased thanks to a group of brave students who stepped in and subdued him - actions that undoubtedly saved lives."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e102172f-8135-421a-a203-53046233e630?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** Jalloh, a naturalized U.S. citizen from Sierra Leone and former Virginia National Guard member, was previously convicted of trying to support ISIS and sentenced to 11 years in prison but was released from custody early in 2024, according to sources. The FBI is investigating the attack as an act of terrorism, with school officials saying there was no longer a threat to staff or students within an hour of the shooting.

* **What happened:** The instructor, a retired military officer, was pronounced dead at the hospital, while the two wounded victims--both Army ROTC members--appear to be in stable condition, with one bringing themselves to the hospital. Old Dominion University President Brian Hemphill said "Old Dominion University faced a tragedy on our main campus" and thanked "the swift response of our police officers, emergency management personnel, and our partners at the City of Norfolk."

name: Forward Party
subject: Why Checks and Balances Still Matter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
For generations, Americans have relied on a simple principle to protect our democracy: no branch of government should hold too much power. But in recent years, that balance has been shifting.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
For generations, Americans have relied on a simple principle to protect our democracy: no branch of government should hold too much power. But in recent years, that balance has been shifting. This week we’re highlighting an important new piece from members of Forward’s Veterans and Military Families Committee: [“The Two‐Party Drift Toward Executive Power.”](https://www.forwardparty.com/media/blog/the-two-party-drift-toward-executive-power/?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_93b&n=1) The article looks at how presidents from both parties have increasingly used military force without meaningful congressional oversight – a trend that raises serious questions about the erosion of constitutional checks and balances. [**__**](https://www.forwardparty.com/media/blog/the-two-party-drift-toward-executive-power/?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_93b&n=2) **_Click the image to read the blog post_** The U.S. Constitution gives Congress the authority to declare war, reflecting the founders’ belief that decisions about military force should involve democratic accountability. But over time, presidents from both parties have increasingly acted without formal congressional approval. The Forward blog argues that the erosion of oversight has made it easier for the executive branch to wield military power with limited restraint. This isn’t just about one president or one party. It reflects a broader pattern in American politics where the two‐party system has allowed power to consolidate in the executive branch while Congress struggles to assert its role. When those checks weaken, so does public confidence in the system. When institutions work properly, power is balanced and decisions carry broader legitimacy. When those guardrails erode, it becomes easier for any administration — Republican or Democrat — to expand executive authority without sufficient accountability. One of the core ideas behind the Forward movement is that political incentives shape political outcomes. If the system rewards partisan loyalty and discourages independent oversight, we should not be surprised when institutions weaken. That is why Forward supports reforms that strengthen democratic accountability and encourage leaders who are willing to work across differences. Healthy competition in politics leads to stronger institutions. Stronger institutions help preserve the constitutional balance that protects our freedoms. **Please forward this to your friends, family, and coworkers. It helps us introduce them to Forward and to what we are building. Also consider inviting them to one of our upcoming events listed below. We'd love to meet them.**
---
---
---
REMINDER: The next episode of The Forward Party Podcast is now live! Drawing on Bob’s experience in public office and grassroots organizing and Sarah’s leadership advocating for veterans and military families, the conversation explores how civic engagement, nonpartisan leadership, and a commitment to community can help rebuild trust in American politics. 53 Senators just gave Trump a blank check.
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127212071/607304347/623074613?code=jtk1442-su-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjJlNTNjMDgtNjMxZS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=PyaJzQYu7KJ6agJyrJBgNx_83yeUWDrtcnqUftFtOZ0=&emci=0c4e5ef3-231e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=b2e53c08-631e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=9329426)
---
Dear friend,

Last week, I stood on the Senate floor and said what I believe to be true: **We are on the precipice of American troops on the ground in Iran.**
As I’m sure you are aware, Donald Trump launched strikes on Tehran without a vote of Congress, without authorization, and clearly without any real strategy. Just days later, Senate Republicans voted to keep it that way.
The War Powers Resolution failed 47 votes to 53. And when Democrats forced every Senator on the record, Republicans chose Trump over the Constitution, with every Republican but one voting to hand Trump a blank check for war.
This isn’t just any procedural vote you hear about. **T****he Constitution is clear: Congress declares war.** Not the one person in the Oval Office. Our Founding Fathers wrote it that way on purpose because they feared exactly what is happening now: an executive who has grown too fond of war-making over diplomacy.
I voted yes. I will keep fighting. I will keep sounding the alarm. And Democrats will force another vote. And another. Until the cost of war, the lives lost, the dollars spent, the constitutional principles being ignored, and the voices around the United States are too much to ignore.
But I need to know the people of Connecticut, and Americans across the nation, are with me. [**Will you sign my petition calling on the Senate to reassert its authority and stop Trump’s unauthorized war in Iran?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127212072/607304350/1388563762?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&amount=5&code=jtk1442-su-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjJlNTNjMDgtNjMxZS1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=PyaJzQYu7KJ6agJyrJBgNx_83yeUWDrtcnqUftFtOZ0=&emci=0c4e5ef3-231e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=b2e53c08-631e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=9329426)

As I’m sure you are aware, Donald Trump launched strikes on Tehran without a vote of Congress, without authorization, and clearly without any real strategy. Just days later, Senate Republicans voted to keep it that way. The War Powers Resolution failed 47 votes to 53. And when Democrats forced every Senator on the record, Republicans chose Trump over the Constitution, with every Republican but one voting to hand Trump a blank check for war. This isn’t just any procedural vote you hear about. The Constitution is clear: Congress declares war. Not the one person in the Oval Office. Friend,

Many in the West -- whether in academia, business, or the media -- prefer to cover their eyes and pretend that totalitarianism isn't spreading.

But if these last five years have shown us anything, it's that totalitarianism is back with a vengeance.

In 2020, China's government was the focus of several new stories:
* Its duplicity around COVID
* The continuing expansion of its surveillance state
* The systematic human rights abuses inflicted on Uyghurs in the Xinjiang region
* The authoritarian crackdown on civil society in Hong Kong, once one of the freest places on earth.

**That 's when Jimmy Lai, along with 53 other democracy proponents in Hong Kong, was imprisoned as part of the Chinese Communist Party's crackdown on dissent.**

Jimmy is an extraordinary man. At 12, he smuggled himself out of mainland China by boat, reaching Hong Kong penniless but ambitious. Sixty years later, his success embodies the entrepreneurial spirit of a free Hong Kong; he built a clothing store empire from nothing, then a newspaper, Apple Daily, and a media conglomerate.

Those accomplishments are impressive, but what he is most passionate about is Hong Kong's democracy movement.

When I interviewed him in November 2020, he said, _" I really appreciate the freedom in Hong Kong. This freedom has given us all that we have. Hope. Inspiration. This is so precious. With my gratitude to this place, it is my duty to do whatever I can to fight for freedom and the rule of law here."_

I'm Brad Lips, CEO of Atlas Network. Atlas Network provides training, grants, and a vital network of peers to pro-freedom organizations wherever they are, even in countries that have suffered under the heavy boot of dictatorship, communist or otherwise.

Jimmy Lai's case should draw worldwide attention to what is being lost in Hong Kong, and in other countries where totalitarianism has taken hold.

When Jimmy Lai spoke virtually at Atlas Network's Liberty Forum in 2020, he shared words that capture the essence of his choice:
_" My life is about something more than myself. . . . **Once I started to fight for freedom, my life changed. I feel there is a purpose and meaning in my life**. Even if I have to go to jail, which is very likely, I don't regret it. I consider it a redemption of the life that I have had. I am prepared for anything."_

That was a year before Jimmy Lai began his time in jail.

From billionaire to political prisoner, Jimmy Lai chose freedom over fortune. Now, 77, he spends the late years of his life behind bars. As you read this, Jimmy Lai spends 23 hours per day in solitary confinement.

Jimmy Lai gave up his life as a billionaire for the cause of liberty.

But his sacrifice is more than a story about Hong Kong.

**It is a universal reminder that the price of freedom is high, and that courage in defense of principle can inspire people everywhere who cherish liberty.**

His example endures as a beacon for all who long to be free, and a reminder that liberty's defenders, no matter the cost, light the way for us all.

Atlas Network plays a vital role in that effort by strengthening the institutions and leaders who carry these ideas forward.

clean_body: Stand against the CCP Many in the West — whether in academia, business, or the media — prefer to cover their eyes and pretend that totalitarianism isn’t spreading. Friend, Many in the West -- whether in academia, business, or the media -- prefer to cover their eyes and pretend that totalitarianism isn't spreading. But if these last five years have shown us anything, it's that totalitarianism is back with a vengeance. In 2020, China's government was the focus of several new stories: Its duplicity around COVID The continuing expansion of its surveillance state The systematic human rights abuses inflicted on Uyghurs in the Xinjiang region The authoritarian crackdown on civil society in Hong Kong, once one of the freest places on earth. That 's when Jimmy Lai, along with 53 other democracy proponents in Hong Kong, was imprisoned as part of the Chinese Communist Party's crackdown on dissent. Jimmy is an extraordinary man. At 12, he smuggled himself out of mainland China by boat, reaching Hong Kong penniless but ambitious. Sixty years later, his success embodies the entrepreneurial spirit of a free Hong Kong; he built a clothing store empire from nothing, then a newspaper, Apple Daily, and a media conglomerate. Those accomplishments are impressive, but what he is most passionate about is Hong Kong's democracy movement. When I interviewed him in November 2020, he said, " I really appreciate the freedom in Hong Kong. This freedom has given us all that we have. Hope. Inspiration. This is so precious. With my gratitude to this place, it is my duty to do whatever I can to fight for freedom and the rule of law here." I'm Brad Lips, CEO of Atlas Network. Atlas Network provides training, grants, and a vital network of peers to pro-freedom organizations wherever they are, even in countries that have suffered under the heavy boot of dictatorship, communist or otherwise. Jimmy Lai's case should draw worldwide attention to what is being lost in Hong Kong, and in other countries where totalitarianism has taken hold. You can help Atlas Network create a world where the norms of free societies, including free speech and the rule of law, are respected. When Jimmy Lai spoke virtually at Atlas Network's Liberty Forum in 2020, he shared words that capture the essence of his choice: " My life is about something more than myself. . . . Once I started to fight for freedom, my life changed. I feel there is a purpose and meaning in my life. Even if I have to go to jail, which is very likely, I don't regret it. I consider it a redemption of the life that I have had. I am prepared for anything." That was a year before Jimmy Lai began his time in jail. From billionaire to political prisoner, Jimmy Lai chose freedom over fortune. Now, 77, he spends the late years of his life behind bars. As you read this, Jimmy Lai spends 23 hours per day in solitary confinement. Jimmy Lai gave up his life as a billionaire for the cause of liberty. But his sacrifice is more than a story about Hong Kong. It is a universal reminder that the price of freedom is high, and that courage in defense of principle can inspire people everywhere who cherish liberty. His example endures as a beacon for all who long to be free, and a reminder that liberty's defenders, no matter the cost, light the way for us all. Atlas Network plays a vital role in that effort by strengthening the institutions and leaders who carry these ideas forward. name: Matias, United We Dream
subject: 🎬 4 Movies to make meaning of the now together!
body:
“Cinema can show the truth with a human depth that numbers and news articles can’t.” - Wesam Hamada | | | Hey Peter, when was the last time a movie brought you hope? Joy? Curiosity? 👀 Despite what you might’ve heard from Timmy over the weekend, there’s so much to learn and appreciate about the art around us. Films, like many forms of art, have the potential to carry powerful messages and help us make meaning of difficult times. **With the Oscars coming up this weekend, our team compiled a list of nominated films that you need to watch with your loved ones: Frankenstein, The Voice of Hind Rajab, Sinners, and The Secret Agent.** We’re living through a moment of uncertainty, but these films call on us to reflect on what really matters: community, resistance, and solidarity. Ready for your next watch party with friends? We’ve put together activities and conversation starters for you and your loved ones to have meaningful discussions about what these movies reveal about the moment we face. 👉 **Text****“MOVIE NIGHT”****to 787-57,[or click this link on your phone today](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.jTd4CJP2oHMhBHdrjS9uuhyHt20_8IkC4i_diP93IzsHV0g8A7QInSSUvCc3-Yz8CKi8nJ3HFaIhkDqJJgz-aHe0yfSHqd57F4LQ6FoGZmYC4v5NkVS3AiPiWzdYI-795pldG7R5r5RgRAKSmIa7hTqxyLH0Wv3cBWtZQCnAGL-dfZXnSh58I08k833GKg9Lr41zOWcEPIsh-copBamBjen-jW_opMi8l7OG9zrwd3IDnfUi_-tdhin8pBpCbiWEEU8N4E56w0VYan_AeOPu6zRMwcjlNmkGOV2NG-IPT69QpKkOCGFywGaklD10WIGJ/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h0/h001.FTPHZ-cOP7m63FPdFGOfhO5kQv7dAXIZB2067N7ZwkU), to prepare for your next watch party with friends! ** **** **🎬 Frankenstein:** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.jTd4CJP2oHMhBHdrjS9uuhyHt20_8IkC4i_diP93IzsjyliosoS3TphJZTwUS164QzEbM6GP6tcrCevz7SlMIJpERhKVfvwX_yBpAM-F_ksLiCWpDAZ2Aqrc88_LkSadQYyhyzlEPfhKC-cIWog5Ft5r_8VwRf6YrIrJR_YDvUJsqklZLpKLvMbUTaBNdm2YyYUG_ylsrElZVsvxSOvqKcd6YdxDFWSO3_-M8Jt0RX9b1AWcTwrL7vrGyt3YNhSXOtcv9CqqA75mTTypoGsGO_5_IgUczH5X8VkmoWQ38cNGEsfbRTV0sYPYLoWSs9CH/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h1/h001.EZTtG1FSx8cMKwBBc73Yy_K64jAgsqPLGLtZ2ZQQyAo)
**What it is about:****__** Driven by ambition and grief over his mother’s death, scientist Victor Frankenstein sets out to conquer death and succeeds in bringing a Creature to life. This leads to dire consequences for both the creator and his creation. **Why watch it now:** “Can we see each other as being part of the same thing? Can we recognize that there is no ‘they’ — there is nothing but us?” In this adaptation of Mary Shelley’s 1818 gothic novel, [director Guillermo del Toro](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMWn3R7U15hZOprFI75oZg45fnuq_NMDAvCUyN08wRUpNBzZFP-IDeImLR2t8rsLpFwESjvdu6eOrhDNAjOGwzqR94TsHu9t9Gi-_YI2cBrjmXHD_ZHClp_4TZ4W9Anxh32frnPK78inxMIWGeU5No4zooPa6DavxF99Tq1IIMmsQjeCLDc9eTM1uQiBO5cfa75-GuPXYOXIXc6HnA-zUR00hWB1GzBI9I9O_14Q31MceRrTBjBfPmgIUbeTCe5Gne172HMgIpc0fxo4QCHZDz61OMlRs-tVsFxawgXzT-ExZnTNy8ZNLu6BYGEt-foA3JA/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h2/h001.rIpxfm2sZvknYZKGnqozwXzNshTlmBE-dAKksLs4SSI) invites us to reflect on what makes us human. In a moment where most of us are struggling to make ends meet, and our freedoms are on the line, _Frankenstein_ challenges us to focus on all that unites us. As [actor Oscar Isaac](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMWn3R7U15hZOprFI75oZg46ru2pjgp3S9mAKz78e-ngkMx4wNwmRfcByBcGgWt9oT0h4bd_cNSObM06olw43HzGyGRogtyV_efBE9lSJ2nItW8qdSvXIJ8bfLIFGsR_Cq0qzQstk04reWq2ID1CAj8cDJxJUz8YfB7Vw_RQqTgJMCfbhcekRl27ToZ_Xl2rwa_ftv9JrWM-p4w9UuaDpV4rpZbbqryt-c0JQkzSBg1SXOPKJXdR6wSRqwymgctr-RCMBxGfDjFBvSVnb_q5ZFuzR_MXr3GL7Ae6_gJC1P-FGhvP-gFg2i_c5bx6cupP7v-Ujmms19tIhT94wouHQcFQ/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h3/h001.1cdmw-3RRCubxHaVW9yfFZS8nV0-PhwVqeRIyPkzurI), who plays Victor, put it: this is a story told by a Guatemalan, an Australian, and a Mexican immigrant.
**🎬 The Voice of Hind Rajab**

[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.jTd4CJP2oHMhBHdrjS9uuhyHt20_8IkC4i_diP93IzvdAbfrUA6a_iRPxaLTiKD8IxgmY-nf97G9Ibb_UKTixdajTvMl_o08iGOsTCwiwmDdYyDn1xwBjcmdXkm8kTrUeGiQSP6t80qZn4CJmMBvLwtLtiE4nZWPYJHZvhhG79y6fmHjefK_2STJZ-Jlan70jU9P5XpnsM3SrtOpXfL3mKQNEnBz7egpIIbUuGmLM4wt3r8wnz6dBbwW14qXNZTz2oMctRPnSzQwzKPMl52AVy4ggNNNWiG2y1K-pjM0RPO7n4DAsb3H3M9aSM9dMq9P/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h4/h001.nF2VsLD3isHlv2YlMdacMyuAA4qJCOqw9UP6pfbTYUw) **What it is about:** Told from the perspective of the dispatchers who tried to save her life, this docudrama recounts the death of 5-year-old Palestinian Hind Rajab at the hands of Israeli forces. **Why watch it now:****__** What does solidarity look like beyond words? This documentary serves as a painful, yet powerful, reminder of the human cost of genocide. “It’s a call for accountability and for justice, because if we don't have accountability and justice, we don't have peace,” [says director Kaouther Ben Hania.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.SEgofQhSb9pGg8bz5XQG3RPUREjDxu6kbfKQ1L-3TYEyQDffgKVtc3m4hDt-gnt7fiKWXIqmK0EkWf8pKnSisW6RZkLgDuYyeL6PWZ05TRAbiEga4ZL9pGv5TGkMubIeAKCtvNsgBabw2uHTJOrc5KfGUYcjTCO0uNnQRlnpDZuzYdP-hrQ41KpiVGufhwlOY9Vd59aJ0Dvu1V1USjWrsRNxVG2105xSyv8G2smL_6ogwEF5JgPDrGAqPawl073Mqv8y8LRYcFxWFWWV6f1EgQRLb93sDlScHHCktXSLl8iKnq3ou4Gy4u-H0KmHDo5sfNETA5RVUrjaaTka00b033YQKFNv0-ABujsuiApqYn5AgmgKZ6xJqCiBziKkWYTK/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h5/h001.Rw5vbijp5oG4WNTXnFjijnC1NbuyhClyiXVHflTUkdA) This movie can be an opportunity to discuss with friends the ways in which we respond to injustice and show solidarity to one another. “My purpose was to make [Hind Rajab’s] voice echo beyond the circle of people who agree with me.”
**🎬 Sinners**
[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.jTd4CJP2oHMhBHdrjS9uuhyHt20_8IkC4i_diP93IzuPfrj9yyoL2P8EeGPbsyLDNUMHji_lVZKaDRjt2JEqnBgxvhXdgLkRBkezfL3ztFu4FtYIEwvPe_tdLAva5Bc_ODGBnpqbhC70OpoSFvfCk08zBOTbZICVJ4x_T0nWn66XTSQ5V5NMrYwIgi2wRsENhOLthQ-BlpK5BSnnQGV7qH4AOsQYixTNJfr-elT8GYs3jy4CO5U6_iEFPKkfjBljhdFf_GbDa6c89deUes70stT9ZC0GIFSuK8hbPIfOga5pUW-OJQgaBj-UTUjcK9KM/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h6/h001.HgNGYwtl6S_3WqOUhCwEQqnSbMl6L7qJAyz67q78Rq8)
**What it is about:****__** Trying to leave their troubled lives behind, twin brothers Elijah and Elias Moore (Smoke and Stack) return to Mississippi in the 1930s with plans to open a juke joint but are confronted by supernatural vampires. **Why watch it now:****__**_Sinners_ is a history lesson on racial injustice, oppression, and the threat of white supremacy. But, at its core, this story is a celebration of Black culture, resistance, and community — and the freedom we find in one another. As [activist Carlton Mackey](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.jTd4CJP2oHMhBHdrjS9uuoSYrSEw-jcVDM4jHpQk4pLidoI6M5-GaWYriO0V3vM7vEHqHop5ZoRcRkNVv1sICAfIG5g4-yXMC33yxuBH3ozpD7679l45Db99JIGTfHyZLDR-myMIfizztr6eEN3lA0zxIwNSwepnJM_URp9NQAxiStpO_voHm3dUQ6QAZUB2viQ1wu0OQBuCKMJ1DV2C61n7_bp6Yl53woyVMJutv06a0t7wCVtPQWHsfrsgJQ8Kr0Ap2jb-MwY0r4VOpRZfcjTzqRku-FB3BlFSM41_j_Qs6yAef2fzZIw8QTo9gDYdpDo9BJ7NqdCnmbQdy7OTmxjSINW5v8BCI7W6UwvQ87PgPBJV2zQ-ZXwNvOAVdAQE/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h7/h001.3TTF2iTGgRY-Gz0_b7rZNmKzhMKS3Ljt1ROFpCnG5FA) describes, “ _Sinners_ teaches us that even in the belly of the beast, there is song. Even in the shadow of death, there is rhythm. And even in a world that tries to steal our breath, we will laugh. We will love. We will rise.”
**🎬 The Secret Agent:**
[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.jTd4CJP2oHMhBHdrjS9uuhyHt20_8IkC4i_diP93Izv44cVcjWagKZOKkDZXJ-KJX4Bl7Vif10W11mTZ8cZWyjK0yc2UCn26SXyd_rhM25xB2gHuNywJszgIauA2y2Nk6G3EuLUF2Xn2BO9dC_9aLmzexbQyDG0VN7Y15Bs2ETw0XqgaOdEwWcGHPm0fO4-XJlgn0j6AwDSvv_5Vb2zXocNcv9l5hfczgUp2N0yWLgCC6_dCOrU4yutYQc5YBM1wALuYDpBAREYAryHIT5NraHIvTnSMXBBu4tM6zBCdI6oOWxrxkYVzhc1v_kdF6Z3P/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h8/h001.WQnOeAomBy7J9uyIUmGMzBYwGLYOZG4vKCTnfkC30mQ)
**What it is about:****__** Armando is a research scientist who arrives in Recife in 1977, during Brazil’s military dictatorship, to reunite with his son before fleeing the country. The film features time-jumps to the present time as historians try to make sense of this historical moment. **Why watch it now:** The Secret Agent forces us to confront the long-lasting impact of authoritarianism and systemic corruption. It highlights the importance of remembering our past and warns us of the danger of allowing the rich and powerful to divide and stifle us. “I think this film is about how to stick with your values when everything around you is saying the opposite of what you think, especially when you are talking about a dictatorship or an authoritarian regime,” shared [actor Wagner Moura,](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMSQ3mboNP_jB5mJMHZsTkfyVYAkNV8lvnR4o-fmL0NZcS2nuOfL5mXmclIRorG0srEJsWL6WgttpHOyrRBx0HIbUL3ljSVEpEbyUIdC-FLzc3MtikeR9iKkscX2RRPZqgFWcfCuR69ioLOwie7SkNm9X6EdJjqRUfAUq0xJ0sO-FDlzaxc4IesJG9XcMsBmcumUWxaQ3WI3uuVrJRx8C9x9arKHRGoAH7tY6sONwm9F-9E_oFiSHJtSuA5AoT5sQ-_SUuO4FUZwRbkEWAl-JetSFEySqLfwvlOI4ceBpD2TMaxwr7KEcGV97wp67ICWmiI0ICFAT7rRhEQxfexpPIfcbDYOGWFTs5EOJc0QwBPUIoPYv7IkLvtG13qjILYq01Q/4ov/WEx2IUcJTSiKYGvtTdCWzg/h9/h001.raTDMBFBDos7B2onlE64C7fQ4IsPTQWDyaXxOfGPrKs) who plays Armando. Peter, this moment is meant to divide and crush us. But finding community — whether it be through watching or discussing our favorite movies together — is our key to protecting one another. clean_body: “Cinema can show the truth with a human depth that numbers and news articles can’t.” - Wesam Hamada | | | Hey Peter, when was the last time a movie brought you hope? Joy? Curiosity? 👀 Despite what you might’ve heard from Timmy over the weekend, there’s so much to learn and appreciate about the art around us. Films, like many forms of art, have the potential to carry powerful messages and help us make meaning of difficult times. With the Oscars coming up this weekend, our team compiled a list of nominated films that you need to watch with your loved ones: Frankenstein, The Voice of Hind Rajab, Sinners, and The Secret Agent. We’re living through a moment of uncertainty, but these films call on us to reflect on what really matters: community, resistance, and solidarity. Ready for your next watch party with friends? We’ve put together activities and conversation starters for you and your loved ones to have meaningful discussions about what these movies reveal about the moment we face. 👉 Text“MOVIE NIGHT”to 787-57,, to prepare for your next watch party with friends! ** 🎬 Frankenstein: What it is about:** Driven by ambition and grief over his mother’s death, scientist Victor Frankenstein sets out to conquer death and succeeds in bringing a Creature to life. This leads to dire consequences for both the creator and his creation. Why watch it now: “Can we see each other as being part of the same thing? Can we recognize that there is no ‘they’ — there is nothing but us?” In this adaptation of Mary Shelley’s 1818 gothic novel, invites us to reflect on what makes us human. In a moment where most of us are struggling to make ends meet, and our freedoms are on the line, Frankenstein challenges us to focus on all that unites us. As , who plays Victor, put it: this is a story told by a Guatemalan, an Australian, and a Mexican immigrant. 🎬 The Voice of Hind Rajab What it is about: Told from the perspective of the dispatchers who tried to save her life, this docudrama recounts the death of 5-year-old Palestinian Hind Rajab at the hands of Israeli forces. Why watch it now: What does solidarity look like beyond words? This documentary serves as a painful, yet powerful, reminder of the human cost of genocide. “It’s a call for accountability and for justice, because if we don't have accountability and justice, we don't have peace,” This movie can be an opportunity to discuss with friends the ways in which we respond to injustice and show solidarity to one another. “My purpose was to make [Hind Rajab’s] voice echo beyond the circle of people who agree with me.” 🎬 Sinners What it is about: Trying to leave their troubled lives behind, twin brothers Elijah and Elias Moore (Smoke and Stack) return to Mississippi in the 1930s with plans to open a juke joint but are confronted by supernatural vampires. Why watch it now:Sinners is a history lesson on racial injustice, oppression, and the threat of white supremacy. But, at its core, this story is a celebration of Black culture, resistance, and community — and the freedom we find in one another. As describes, “ Sinners teaches us that even in the belly of the beast, there is song. Even in the shadow of death, there is rhythm. And even in a world that tries to steal our breath, we will laugh. We will love. We will rise.” 🎬 The Secret Agent: What it is about: Armando is a research scientist who arrives in Recife in 1977, during Brazil’s military dictatorship, to reunite with his son before fleeing the country. The film features time-jumps to the present time as historians try to make sense of this historical moment. Why watch it now: The Secret Agent forces us to confront the long-lasting impact of authoritarianism and systemic corruption. It highlights the importance of remembering our past and warns us of the danger of allowing the rich and powerful to divide and stifle us. “I think this film is about how to stick with your values when everything around you is saying the opposite of what you think, especially when you are talking about a dictatorship or an authoritarian regime,” shared who plays Armando. Peter, this moment is meant to divide and crush us. But finding community — whether it be through watching or discussing our favorite movies together — is our key to protecting one another. If you’re looking for your next watch, consider gathering your loved ones to watch one of these films together. Will you check out our list of movies today, and share it with your friends online? | | | | | | | In unity, Matias and the United We Dream team Follow us on: | | | | |

body:
War impacts Wisconsin farmers
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260312-2602)
Peter,
Just as Wisconsin farmers are getting ready to plant, the price of fertilizer is spiking because of an illegal war.
Urea — the most common nitrogen fertilizer — is up 25% since the end of February. Diesel is climbing. And because the Strait of Hormuz is effectively shut down, a third of the world's fertilizer trade is stuck on the water.
A Waukesha County farmer told [FOX6](https://act.francescahong.com/go/5446?t=1&akid=2602%2E105371%2Ehe9laE) yesterday: "I don't get a check every week. I don't get that check until I sell that product. And I don't know what that cost is going to be. But I know that fertilizers are going to cost me more, seed's going to cost me more, fuel is going to cost me more.”
Here's what that means for the rest of us: Fertilizer goes up. Farmers cut back or eat the loss. And by late summer, we’re paying more for staples like milk, bread and meat — for everything that has to be grown and everything that has to be shipped.
Nationally, analysts say farmers may shift over a million acres from corn to soybeans this spring because corn takes too much fertilizer to pencil out. Wisconsin planted 3.75 million acres of corn last year, most of it feed for our dairy herds. Less corn means higher feed costs. Higher feed costs mean higher milk prices.
This war is costing Wisconsin — it’s already hitting us at the gas pump, and soon it will be impacting us at the grocery checkout. The question is, who will be hit hardest? Right now, it's farmers and working families. It doesn't have to be this way.
We must end this disastrous war. And at home, we must create a tax system where wealthy people and corporations pay their share, so family farmers and working people aren't carrying the load alone. And we need a governor who shows up in every county and listens to the people who grow our food.
**[Learn more about our policies here.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/440?t=2&akid=2602%2E105371%2Ehe9laE)**

In solidarity,
Fran

Peter,

While the rise in popularity of politicians like Zohran Mamdani and his socialist policies might have come as a shock to many, I've been warning people about it for years.

Younger Americans do not know what socialism means.

When younger Americans think of "socialism," they think it means Sweden and Denmark.

They didn't grow up during the Cold War. They don't remember the Soviet Union. Or Stalin's Gulags or the Warsaw Pact. They couldn't even tell you what the initials U.S.S.R. stood for, or that Nazi is the abbreviation of National Socialist.

**Young Americans need to hear about socialism, real socialism, from someone who experienced it firsthand. I can think of no one better than Ayn Rand.**

Rand wrote novels like _We The Living_ , which dramatized the inhumanity of the Soviet system -- and most importantly, _Atlas Shrugged_ , which dramatized what would happen if socialism came to America. Rand's immense success in making the moral case for capitalism led my friend, the late Ed Crane, to call her "the greatest all-time recruiter for the liberty movement."

The challenge is that young people simply aren't reading novels anymore. In the 70s, 70% of young people read fiction daily for fun -- today, less than 12% do.

That's where The Atlas Society comes in. They bring Ayn Rand's ideas to life for new audiences in innovative ways, including animated videos, viral social media, graphic novels -- even music videos. Plus online courses and live events.

I told Jennifer Grossman, The Atlas Society's CEO, that I would help her raise $30,000 online this month to introduce more young minds to Ayn Rand's ideas.

clean_body: Peter, While the rise in popularity of politicians like Zohran Mamdani and his socialist policies might have come as a shock to many, I've been warning people about it for years. Younger Americans do not know what socialism means. When younger Americans think of "socialism," they think it means Sweden and Denmark. They didn't grow up during the Cold War. They don't remember the Soviet Union. Or Stalin's Gulags or the Warsaw Pact. They couldn't even tell you what the initials U.S.S.R. stood for, or that Nazi is the abbreviation of National Socialist. Young Americans need to hear about socialism, real socialism, from someone who experienced it firsthand. I can think of no one better than Ayn Rand. Rand wrote novels like We The Living , which dramatized the inhumanity of the Soviet system -- and most importantly, Atlas Shrugged , which dramatized what would happen if socialism came to America. Rand's immense success in making the moral case for capitalism led my friend, the late Ed Crane, to call her "the greatest all-time recruiter for the liberty movement." The challenge is that young people simply aren't reading novels anymore. In the 70s, 70% of young people read fiction daily for fun -- today, less than 12% do. That's where The Atlas Society comes in. They bring Ayn Rand's ideas to life for new audiences in innovative ways, including animated videos, viral social media, graphic novels -- even music videos. Plus online courses and live events. I told Jennifer Grossman, The Atlas Society's CEO, that I would help her raise $30,000 online this month to introduce more young minds to Ayn Rand's ideas. Otherwise, please let me explain why I believe The Atlas Society and its leadership are best suited to combat the rise in popularity of these harmful ideologies. First, Jennifer and I go back more than 35 years, when she was a White House Speechwriter, and Americans for Tax Reform was in its founding era. She's one of the most innovative, effective, and persevering executives I know. Over the past decade, she's built The Atlas Society into a juggernaut for freedom. The Atlas Society is the ONLY non-profit adapting Rand 's works into media that appeals to young Americans. Just one example: their animated book trailer for Atlas Shrugged drew 12 million views, and DOUBLED sales of the novel! They're currently producing a full-length feature film of Anthem, Rand's dystopian novella. I believe in their great work because I've seen the impact they've had. It's why I've collaborated with The Atlas Society on various discussions and interviews, including speaking at their student conferences, doing interviews on their podcast, and even doing stand-up comedy at one of their fundraising galas! Thank you, Grover Norquist P.S. If you still aren't convinced, let me tell you what will happen if young Americans fail to learn these important lessons. Without a moral philosophy based on reason, achievement, individualism, and freedom, the next generation will continue to embrace socialism and a culture of envy, entitlement, victimhood, and resentment. She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260312em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260312em]
Let’s be clear about what that means.
It means placing the administration of our elections under the personal control of a President who has already tried to overturn one election. And it means ripping up our Constitution because our wannabe dictator doesn’t like the results of an election he clearly lost. And it’s a clear signal he’s afraid of losing more elections and the accountability that will follow.
I won’t allow that to happen in Oregon.
States run elections. Not presidents. And as Oregon’s Secretary of State, I take that responsibility seriously — because democracy doesn’t defend itself.
We’ve beaten Trump-backed efforts in court before. We’ve already stopped him from forcing Oregon to give his Department of Justice access to your private voter data. And if he tries again, we’ll fight him again — and win again.
So here’s the bottom line: Trump can bluster on right-wing podcasts and cable news all he wants. He can threaten, lie, cheat, and moan about all the elections he’s lost.
But in Oregon, the rules still matter. The Constitution still matters. And intimidation will always fail.
I can’t do this alone, though. Taking on President Donald Trump and winning requires a strong grassroots network, so I’m asking you to stand with me and add your name to my petition today. This isn’t about party allegiance. This is about whether we let a would-be dictator decide who gets to vote and who wins elections.
I know where I stand. I’m counting on you to be there with me.
Thank you,
Tobias Read

body:

---
Peter,

We always knew Jon Husted could be bought, but this is especially appalling. Take a look:
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6995?t=6&akid=737%2E124072%2ErglVRN)
Here are the facts: **New reports reveal that my opponent, Jon Husted, has taken 10x more money than any U.S. senator from billionaire Leslie Wexner. Wexner is a longtime associate of Jeffrey Epstein and one of his co-conspirators.**
It gets worse. Husted didn’t just take Wexner’s money.

When the Senate had the chance to release the Epstein files and provide accountability for the victims, **Husted voted against it.**
Wexner’s most recent donation to Husted came _just a few weeks before that vote._ You do the math.
It all makes me sick to my stomach.

Ohioans deserve transparency. We deserve accountability.
**We deserve a senator who fights for working people, not one who protects the rich and powerful. Not one who protects the Epstein class. Not one who protects pedophiles.**
I've spent my career holding powerful interests accountable – and I'm fighting as hard as I can to unseat Jon Husted and prove that working people, justice, and accountability matter more than protecting billionaires.

But no one person could win this fight alone. I need you, Peter.
**If you believe the super wealthy shouldn’t get special treatment – and the truth shouldn’t be hidden –[I’m asking you to split $5 or whatever you can today to help us flip Ohio and bring accountability back to the Senate.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6995?t=7&akid=737%2E124072%2ErglVRN)**
Thank you.

In solidarity,

Sherrod Brown

Peter,

**House Republicans are at it again.** This time, Rep. Andy Ogles of Tennessee is talking about banning Muslims from entering the United States.

As a Muslim, a Philadelphian, and a candidate for Congress, let me be clear: _Muslims are not the problem. Immigrants are not the problem._

**The real problem is politicians who would rather stir up Islamophobia, bigotry, and division than actually do the job they were elected to do.**

Instead of lowering costs or helping working families get ahead, they’re pushing failed policies and trying to distract us with hate.

Costs are still too high for families. Groceries, health care, and utilities keep rising. And their reckless agenda — from tariffs that raise prices to immigration crackdowns that make our communities less safe — has done nothing to solve the real problems Americans are facing.

Islamophobia and bigotry have real consequences. Words like these fuel division and put Muslim communities at risk.

**That’s why I’ve fought to push forward hate crimes legislation and stand up against Islamophobia and bigotry — and it’s why I’ll keep doing that in Congress.**

Muslims are part of the fabric of this country. Our neighbors, coworkers, and friends.

| Hi folks,

I’m Nadia Rahman, and I recently joined Saikat Chakrabarti’s campaign as Political Director.

I am writing to you personally because something very exciting is happening in San Francisco right now — the momentum is building.

In the last few weeks alone:

* Saikat’s interview with **Hasan Piker** reached millions of people who are hungry for a new kind of politics.
* We’ve seen huge volunteer turnout across the city, with **hundreds of people** showing up to knock doors, organize events, and help build this campaign from the ground up.
* And today, we’re excited to share that two organizations have **officially endorsed Saikat’s campaign** in the last week.

These endorsements reflect the kind of movement we’re building:

| **California College Democrats**
As the largest statewide network of student Democrats, CCD members are committed to building a California that works for students, working families, and communities across our state.

These young people also know all too well what it feels like to watch years of half-measures and empty promises from a Democratic Party more focused on corporate donors than delivering for working families.

**Health Care for All – California**
Health Care for All has been at the forefront of the movement to guarantee universal health care through single-payer financing.

Saikat is proud to stand with them in calling for Medicare for All — because in the richest country in the world, health care should be a right, not a privilege.

---

These endorsements matter, but what matters even more is the grassroots movement growing around this campaign.
**Every week, I see new volunteers stepping up. Students, workers, longtime San Franciscans — people who believe we deserve leadership willing to challenge the political establishment and fight for working people.**

The establishment may have their corporate donors and insider networks, but they can never match the energy and power of organized people.

If you want to be part of what we’re building, we’d love to have you involved.
